newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela names bidders for state banks.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela names bidders for state banks.

text.p: Venezuela's state Deposits Guarantee Fund, Fogade, said it had received deposits from seven banks interested in bidding in Thursday's auctions for state banks Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado.

Fogade President Esther de Margulis told a news conference that Spain's Banco Santander, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya and a group led by Colombia's Banco de Bogota had registered to bid for Banco de Venezuela, which has been valued at $286 million.
The same three groups plus Chile's Infisa CA had registered to bid for Banco Consolidado, valued at $148 million, de Margulis said.
Six banks had originally qualified to bid for Banco de Venezuela and 13 for Banco Consolidado.
"With the privatization of these banks we will be able to say an important part of the financial crisis is over," Margulis said.
The closing date for applications for a 20 percent stake in each bank made available to small shareholders was also on Tuesday.
For Banco de Venezuela, about 4,000 potential shareholders had offered 14 billion bolivars ($29.5 million), which would be about 10 percent of the bank, de Margulis said.
For Banco Consolidado orders from 1,000 potential shareholders worth about 5 billion bolivars ($10.5 billion), or roughly six percent of the bank, were received.
The winning bidders in Thursday's auctions will have until January 17 to take up an option to buy the remaining shares not taken up by small investors from Fogade.
This will be Fogade's second attempt to sell Banco de Venezuela. An earlier auction was abandoned at the last minute in August over legal uncertainties.

But de Margulis stressed on Tuesday that the auctions would now go ahead. "All the legal actions which have been taken against the sale of the banks are totally false and have no legal basis," she said.
Fogade inherited the two banks in August 1994 when they collapsed during a financial sector crisis that affected over half of the commercial banking sector.
Banco de Venezuela is Venezuela's second largest bank in terms of deposits. Banco Consolidado is the fourth largest.
